title: First Lesson: Fetch
intro_lines: Puck worries a splintered oar handle, tail going.
You whistle.
It tilts its head, unimpressed. Fetch, then.

choices.label: Throw the oar into the shallows

outcomes.text: Puck belly-flops after it and drags it back, insufferably proud.
It brings back a rotten coconut instead. Close enough for a first try.
It misjudges a wave, tumbles, and sulks in the foam until you apologise.
The bargain holds. Puck learns fast when it is being paid.
It eats the bribe, then ignores the oar entirely and sleeps.

choices.label: Skip the lesson, let it nap

outcomes.text: It sleeps against your boot. Trust grows in the quiet.
You both lose the afternoon to the heat and learn nothing.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk tamed feral kid goats on Juan Fernández for milk and company, the same patient bribery that turns a wild animal into a working partner.

title: The Buried Locker
intro_lines: Puck's nose drops.
It digs with both forefeet.
Sand sprays your shins. It will not be stopped.

outcomes.text: A tarred bundle: sailcloth, a flint striker, a dead man's boots.
Older bones. A turtle's ribs, picked clean, and a shell worth keeping.
You strike rusted iron and open your palm on it.

choices.label: Let Puck dig alone, hands off

outcomes.text: It presents a pearl as though it were a fish head, all pride.
It hoards the find under the floorboards. Yours, apparently, not.

choices.label: Call it off, the bank is unstable

outcomes.text: The dune caves where you stood. Puck presses hard to your leg.
It obeys, resentfully, then digs three fresh holes out of spite.

history_note: Pedro Serrano used shells as rain-catchers and fuel on Serrana Bank, teaching himself to wring use from whatever the tide buried.

title: Bad Fish
intro_lines: Puck vomits seawater and half-digested fish.
Then it curls tight and will not look at you.
The fish that did it was silver, not scaled.

choices.label: Boil herbs into a bitter mash

outcomes.text: It laps the mash, shivers once, and sleeps it off by noon.
It refuses it hot, takes it cold, and recovers slowly and grudgingly.
It heaves the mash back up. You sit the whole night out with it.

choices.label: Force freshwater down it, a sip

outcomes.text: Small sips, then a long drink. Colour comes back to its flanks.
Too fast. It brings the water straight back up on your boots.

choices.label: Let it ride it out. Watch all night

outcomes.text: By dawn it is on its feet, thinner and warier, and follows you closely.
It worsens. You hold its head clear of the sick and count breaths.
It goes still a long moment, then breathes. You do not sleep at all.

history_note: Ciguatera from large reef predators is not destroyed by cooking, so a silver barracuda can poison a companion that eats better than you do.

title: The Crab It Could Not Leave
intro_lines: Puck freezes, quivering, fixed on a crab.
The crab is huge and entirely unbothered.
It bolts before you can grab the harness.

outcomes.text: You corner both. Puck gets the crab, you get the claw and the meat.
The crab escapes. Puck slices a forefoot open on the coral doing it.
You slip in the surf and go down hard on the wet rock.

choices.label: Whistle it back and sit still

outcomes.text: It returns at last, sulking, and leans its whole weight on your shin.
The crab wanders to you instead. Dinner, rudely delivered.
It ignores you for an hour. The crab wins and you look foolish.
Puck learns the trick itself: bait, wait, pounce. A hunter is made.
It eats the bait and abandons the hunt entirely, well fed and useless.

history_note: Coconut crabs climb palms and crush with claws measured near 3,300 newtons, so a companion that chases one is not merely playing.

title: Something on the Treeline
intro_lines: Puck's low rasp wakes you before the sound does.
Something is walking the treeline, unhurried.
Your blade is under the cot. You reach slowly.

choices.label: Send Puck to circle behind it

outcomes.text: It flushes a UTC scout, who runs rather than fight alone in the rain.
It flushes a boar instead. The boar charges straight through your fire.
Puck is gone too long. You find it shaking in the wet ferns.

choices.label: Keep Puck close and build the fire

outcomes.text: Whatever it was decides your fire is not worth the trouble.
It circles twice more, then goes. You do not sleep again.
A shape breaks cover: a UTC scout, who marks your camp and leaves.

choices.label: Go out and meet it alone

outcomes.text: A half-drowned sailor, unarmed. You give him water and a fire.
Nothing out there but a torn sail snapping on a stake.
A boar at close quarters. Puck hits it and buys you one breath.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk tamed feral cats after rats gnawed his feet at night, keeping them as sentinels as much as companions.

title: The Scent Line
intro_lines: Puck works a scent line through the ferns.
Not a wild smell.
Something carried.

outcomes.text: A poacher's snare line, and a pig still warm in the wire.
A tideborn blind, empty, marked with shells. A scout watches, then is gone.
The trail ends at a wallow. The boar is very much at home.

choices.label: Lift Puck and back away downwind

outcomes.text: You withdraw unseen. Puck trembles, then slowly relaxes against you.
Something follows you half the way back to the outpost.

choices.label: Put Puck on a lead and press on

outcomes.text: Leashed, it works the trail cleaner, nose down, no wasted steps.
It fights the rope the whole way and you learn nothing at all.

history_note: Feral pigs left by sailors root up ground and eat crab juveniles and eggs, so their wallows and runs are the clearest trails any island offers.

title: The Hand in the Sand
intro_lines: Puck digs at something under a scrap of canvas.
Not a shell.
The sand there is the wrong shape.

outcomes.text: A hand. Then an arm. The man under the canvas is breathing.
Canvas, wet sand, then a salt-crusted wrist that moves when you touch it.

choices.label: Drag Puck off and mark the spot

outcomes.text: You stake the canvas down and haul Puck home, snarling at your heel.
It fights the harness the whole way back to camp and sleeps facing away.

history_note: On Serrana Bank a second castaway reached Pedro Serrano after years alone, and the two men quarrelled before they made peace, the sea rarely sending help in a shape you want.

title: Diving for Supper
intro_lines: Puck porpoises over the reef crest, hunting.
It dives.
Bubbles, then nothing, then bubbles.

outcomes.text: It hauls up a grouper bigger than its own head and drops it at your feet.
It surfaces with a moray still clamped to its flank.
A reef shark takes the fish out of its jaws and leaves a graze.

choices.label: Call it in before the grey shape returns

outcomes.text: It comes grudging, with two small fish and a rag of net tangled on it.
It ignores you until the shark has passed. Your nerves pay for it.

choices.label: Wade out and fish it yourself

outcomes.text: You spear two. Puck herds them into the shallows and holds them.
You gash a shin open on coral and come back with nothing.

history_note: Reef sharks are drawn by blood and thrashing in the shallows, so a companion diving with a struggling fish is ringing a bell underwater.

title: Salt in the Wound
intro_lines: He is UTC by his coat.
Pressed, not willing.
His hands are bound with his own belt.

choices.label: Cut him loose and give him water

outcomes.text: Pressed off a merchantman. He knows where UTC careens and draws it for you.
He drinks, thanks you, and is gone before dawn. So is your flint.
He drinks, then reaches for your knife. Puck gets to his wrist first.

choices.label: Take his coat and boots, leave the belt

outcomes.text: You walk away with good boots, a warm coat and a bad feeling.
He shouts a ship's name after you. Puck growls at the trees all day.
He works the belt loose and comes at your back. Puck is already turning.

choices.label: Leave water within reach and go

outcomes.text: He is free by nightfall. You never learn his name or his ship.
He is dead by morning. Puck will not leave the spot and will not eat.

history_note: Pirate articles condemned offenders to marooning with a gun, a bottle of water and a bottle of powder, a sentence the sea knows well.

title: What the Tide Left
intro_lines: Puck is gone from the cot.
You find it digging.
The canvas is shredded. Whatever is under it is metal.

outcomes.text: A UTC dark-binding crystal in an iron cage. Puck will not come near it.
A tideborn reliquary, sealed with coral. It hums when you lift it.
Powder, damp and useless, in a crate that stinks of tar and old water.
You cover it and sleep badly. Puck does not dig there again.
It is back at the hole by noon. So, inevitably, are you.

choices.label: Haul it to the water and let it go

outcomes.text: It slides under the surf and does not come back. Puck watches it go.
The rope parts and the crate stays. Puck stares at the water a while.

history_note: Tromelin's castaways kept a single fire alive fifteen years on wreck timber and driftwood and salvaged lead basins for water, wreckage on a beach never being only wreckage.

title: The Yelp on the Cliff
intro_lines: You point Puck up the cliff path.
It goes.
Ten minutes. Then a yelp, cut short.

outcomes.text: A crevice, a dropped fish, and Puck, wedged and furious with you.
You find it cornered in the rocks by something with too many limbs.
The yelp was a gull. Puck is perfectly fine and smug about it.
It comes up the path with a cut foot and a stolen egg in its mouth.
Nothing. You whistle until your throat is raw and the fog thickens.
It bites the rope and you haul it up, sodden, shaking and grateful.
It tangles itself, panics, and you nearly lose the rope and your grip.

history_note: Tromelin's castaways fed on sooty tern colonies numbering tens of thousands, which is why a cliff full of birds is worth a dangerous climb.

title: Goat Kid Jealousy
intro_lines: Tide-Puck snaps at a tamed goat kid.
The kid bleats; Puck guards his bowl.

outcomes.text: Puck learns to share; kid follows you.
Puck sulks for a day, then recovers.
Puck withdraws; kid grows bold.
Puck obeys but sulks at night.

history_note: Selkirk tamed kid goats for milk and company on Juan Fernandez.

title: Puck Turns on the Kid
intro_lines: Puck corners the goat kid at dawn.
Ears flat; snarling low.

outcomes.text: Puck stands down; kid spared.
Kid bolts; Puck chases but stops.
Kid wins respect; Puck backs off.
Kid injured; you treat the wound.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk ran down feral goats on foot on Juan Fernandez and tamed kids for milk and company.

title: Rats in the Larder
intro_lines: Rats gnaw through your stores.
Puck watches, uninterested.

outcomes.text: Puck clears the larder in a night.
Puck plays, rats scatter deeper.
You catch six; stores saved.
Trap springs empty; rats return.

history_note: Rats gnawed Alexander Selkirk's feet as he slept until he tamed feral cats to keep them off.

title: Parrot Learns a Word
intro_lines: A scarlet parrot lands on your shoulder.
It cocks its head, listening.

outcomes.text: It squawks it at passing sails.
It only says 'food' instead.
It returns with a shiny shell.
It flies off, never returns.

history_note: Parrots mimic speech and were sold in pirate havens.

title: Injured Gull
intro_lines: A gull with a broken wing lies in surf.
Puck sniffs, wary of its beak.

outcomes.text: It heals; later circles your camp.
It pecks free and escapes injured.
Crabs take it; Puck sulks all day.
It dies; Puck eats it anyway.

history_note: Tromelin castaways ate sooty terns and seabirds by the colony.

title: Puck Refuses a Command
intro_lines: You strike Puck for eating a coil.
He cowers; refuses your whistle.

outcomes.text: Puck forgives; tail wags again.
He eats but keeps distance.
Puck obeys, then hides for hours.
He snaps; you lose a finger's skin.

history_note: Companion animals reduced despair for Selkirk and Ada Blackjack.

title: Coconut Crab Theft
intro_lines: A coconut crab steals your knife.
Puck tracks it into the rocks.

outcomes.text: Puck corners it; knife recovered.
Claw pinches Puck's nose; retreat.
Crab drops knife, takes coconut.
It ignores you, vanishes seaward.

history_note: Coconut crabs scavenge and steal shiny objects.

title: Training Breakthrough
intro_lines: Puck drags a fish to your feet.
He waits, tail stiff, for praise.

outcomes.text: Puck learns 'fetch fish' reliably.
He eats it before you can praise.
Puck tries again, succeeds.
Puck drops the trick, confused.

history_note: Selkirk read the Bible aloud to keep his speech.

title: Puck Warns of Boar
intro_lines: Puck freezes, hackles raised.
A boar grunts in the ferns.

outcomes.text: You slip away; boar loses interest.
Boar charges; Puck bites its ear.
Boar flees; you gather tusks.
Boar gores your leg; Puck drags you out.

history_note: Feral boar charge when cornered or with piglets.

title: Tide-Puck Finds Fresh Water
intro_lines: Puck scratches at wet sand.
A seep pools behind the dune.

outcomes.text: You fill two skins; Puck drinks first.
Sand collapses; water turns brackish.
Later you find a full pool.
Tide washes it out; spot lost.

history_note: Digging behind the dune line can reach a brackish lens.

title: Puck's Night Watch
intro_lines: Puck won't sleep; stares at surf.
A shape moves in the fog.

outcomes.text: Tideborn scout passes; Puck silent.
UTC patrol; you hide in time.
False alarm; sleep lost, morale drops.
You catch a thief at the stores.

history_note: Selkirk hid from Spanish ships and waited for English.
